[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-03] This facility is attributed in the registry to Stack Infrastructure, or in 3 Milan, Italy rows researched in this same batch, to the shorter operator field spelling STACK. This batch researches both spellings together since both point to the operator branded stackinfra.com in sources fetched this session, but this batch does not merge or rewrite either operator field value, leaving that naming inconsistency on file for a future pass to resolve if desired. STACK Infrastructure was launched January 16, 2019, per a trade press article from datacenterdynamics.com fetched this session, by IPI Partners, described in that article as a joint venture between Iron Point and Iconiq Capital. The new company launched with eight data centers across six United States markets and about 100 MW of capacity, built from two predecessor portfolios, three facilities from Infomart Data Centers in Ashburn Virginia, Portland Oregon, and Silicon Valley California, which IPI Partners had acquired in March 2018 after Equinix bought Infomart own Dallas headquarters building earlier that year, and five facilities from T5 Data Centers, a company IPI Partners had separately backed since 2016, in Atlanta Georgia, Chicago Illinois, and the Dallas Fort Worth Texas area, with T5 Data Centers itself continuing to operate separately afterward with remaining sites in Los Angeles, Charlotte, Colorado Springs, New York, and Cork City Ireland. Brian Cox, previously chief executive of Infomart Data Centers, became STACK Infrastructure own chief executive. STACK Infrastructure own about page, fetched this session, describes the company as a partner designing, developing, and operating global digital infrastructure, and states a current footprint of 10 metro markets in the Americas, 5 in Asia Pacific, and 7 in EMEA, 22 markets in total, though each market can itself include multiple campuses, for example Silicon Valley alone contains 3 campuses and Milan alone contains 11. This registry already carried, prior to this session, one already complete row for an Atlanta, Georgia facility a prior pass in this registry had itself corrected from an operator field of T5 Data Centers to Stack Infrastructure based on a documented 2019 sale, and one already complete row for the New Albany, Ohio facility, one of the original eight launch data centers, both consistent with the acquisition history recorded here and both untouched by this batch. None of the operator own pages fetched this session for the facilities in this batch published a street address, so no row in this batch receives an address field, a reverse geocoding attempt on one representative coordinate this session was again throttled, consistent with a persistent throttle on that service observed repeatedly earlier in this same campaign. This row carries the generic registry name Stack Infrastructure without a specific facility code, and its coordinates place it in Santa Clara County, California, close to a sibling row in this registry carrying the identical generic name at nearly the same coordinates, and a greater distance from the already separately identified STACK SVY02 row also researched in this batch. The operator own Silicon Valley region overview page, fetched this session, states the region contains 3 campuses totaling 150 MW of capacity across 97 acres, of which only SVY01, in San Jose, and SVY02, in Santa Clara, are individually named and detailed, a third campus is referenced only in the regional totals and not separately identified on the pages fetched this session. The operator own dedicated page for SVY01, fetched this session, places it in San Jose, California, and states a 19 acre, 4 building campus, SVY01A through SVY01D, with 100 MW of total capacity and 1,030,000 square feet of data hall space across the 4 buildings, individually 140,000, 240,000, 350,000, and 300,000 square feet respectively, but does not give a street address. Given this row own coordinates are consistent with the San Jose area rather than Santa Clara, and SVY02 is already accounted for by a separate row in this registry, this row is most plausibly one of the 4 SVY01 buildings, though which of the 4 cannot be determined from the operator own pages fetched this session, so no capacity or square footage figure is attributed to this specific row.
